label: the blanket inject clear runs in event-driven mode rather than clocked
equivalent: EQUIVALENT, not a hole, and it is the per-touched clear that makes it so. INVARIANT: `inject` is all-zero at the head of every tick. It holds at construction and after `reset_state`, and it is restored each tick because an entry can only become non-zero through `self.inject[p] += w` in the delivery loop, and that loop pushes `p` onto `touched` whenever it finds `self.inject[p] == 0.0` -- which, by the invariant, is true of the FIRST delivery to `p` in the tick. So every neuron whose `inject` the tick could have written is on `touched` (possibly more than once, when a zero weight or a cancelling pair leaves the running total at zero and a later delivery pushes it again -- that makes the list redundant, never short); `touched` is cleared at the head of the tick and, in event-driven mode, taken and put back before the clear runs; and the end-of-tick loop that writes 0.0 at every index in `touched` therefore zeroes every entry that moved, in BOTH modes. The blanket pass consequently only ever writes 0.0 over entries that are already 0.0, so running it under one mode rather than the other cannot change any value that any read of `inject` returns, in either mode. The external-current scan only ADDS indices to `touched`, so it cannot shorten the clear either. MEASURED with a standalone fixture holding the real `sim` beside the mutated copy, both driven over the same randomised networks -- 20,000 simulations of 2 to 5 neurons, 1 to 9 synapses including zero weights and exactly cancelling pairs, delays 0 to 3, both modes, exact timing on and off, three tick lengths, four refractory periods, 200 to 500 ticks each -- comparing the spike trains, every ledger counter and every membrane potential bit for bit: 0 disagreed.
